judged_text: The new externalId parameter on CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:221, 264-265) is dead weight: it never influences creation and is only echoed into the EventResult, while the service independently re-derives the target calendar from credentialId — two sources of truth for where the event landed; if a provider's internal derivation ever diverges (e.g., the 'primary' fallback), the persisted reference describes a calendar the event isn't in.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, createEvent now accepts an optional externalId (signature change) but never uses it when invoking the provider; it always calls calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id) and only echoes externalId back into the returned EventResult (added fields at the return object). Meanwhile, at least GoogleCalendarService.createEvent independently selects the calendarId from calEventRaw.destinationCalendar by matching credentialId (and falls back to "primary"), meaning the persisted EventResult.externalId can be conceptually redundant or become a second, potentially divergent “source of truth” if the provider selection logic differs from the caller’s passed externalId. This is a concrete diff-grounded design/consistency concern, though a mismatch is not directly proven by the shown call sites.
